$comment: What this server was built against, and the gate that keeps it honest.
@arcnow/sdk is PUBLISHED to npm from arcnow-io/arcnow-io-sdk, one tagged release per
version, and this server depends on it at an EXACT version - never a range, never a
path. The tool descriptions promise what one known SDK does; a `^` would let `npm install`
move the code under them with no commit here saying so. Moving the pin is a pull request.
The maintainers' pin gate enforces four things, with their preflight running it straight after the
install (the install is not a check; it is the gate's subject):
1. package.json depends on sdk.package at exactly sdk.version.
2. package-lock.json's entry for it carries that version, resolves to the npm registry, and
its integrity IS sdk.integrity - the link between the version and the bytes; npm refuses
to install a tarball that does not hash to it.
3. node_modules/@arcnow/sdk/package.json is that version: what the server compiles against.
4. The registry serves that version with that dist.integrity, so the pinned bytes are the
published bytes. Needs the network; unreachable is a WARNING unless
ARCNOW_REQUIRE_REGISTRY=1 (CI), a 404 is always a failure.
THE TARBALL IS THE SURFACE. Until the SDK was published this file hashed its sources file by
file and the gate recompiled its dist/; sdk.integrity, the sha512 of the one tarball every
module, generated ABI and networks.json ship in, replaces all of it. No separate hash of the
installed networks.json is kept: the server reads addresses through the SDK's API, from the
tarball's own copy.
MOVING THE PIN is a commit of its own: `npm install @arcnow/sdk@X.Y.Z --save-exact`, `npm ci`,
the pin gate's --record (records version, integrity and tag from the manifest and the
lockfile, and refuses a version the registry does not have), update sdk.why, run
the preflight, and say in the message what changed in the SDK surface and what it meant
for the tools. A tool description that still promises what an older SDK did is how a model
ends up telling somebody the wrong price.
The forked-chain proof under test/fork/ still runs the PRIVATE arcnow-io/sdk checkout's
fork deployer (a checkout beside this one). That is private infrastructure
for the maintainers' chain gate, not part of this pin, and the ordinary build and tests need
nothing but `npm ci`.

why: @arcnow/sdk 0.2.0: the first release that speaks arcnow.io's LIVE fee-model stack (bonding-curve@4.x)
and the first to carry the Arc MAINNET preset. Moved from 0.1.3 (the retired 3.x multi-quote surface);
0.1.4 and 0.1.5 changed READMEs and doc comments, no exported surface. It pins arcnow-io/contracts main
e461106 (bonding-curve@4, curve-factory@4, platform-config@4, platform-registry@4, arc-now-fee-hook@4,
token-factory@2; launchpad@3, quote-registry@1, migrator-registry@1.1, uniswap-v4-migrator@2 unchanged).
Its networks.json records TWO deployments, both live, both read by this server through resolveNetwork:
arc-mainnet (chain 5042, rpc.mainnet.arc.io, deployed at block 21179866): launchpad 0xae1e5558...9dae3,
arcnowPlatform 0xe3c7cd3e...b2ef9, v4 PoolManager 0x8366a39c..., router 0x4a142209..., EURC
0xbef5f6d5...21c1 (6 decimals) among its quoteTokens - REAL MONEY; and arc-testnet (chain 5042002,
deployed at block 62386232): launchpad 0x675a7a60...9d952, arcnowPlatform 0x912898e5...8f4a4, EURC
0x89b50855...9d72a. THIS SERVER RESTATES NO ADDRESS: it reads them from the preset ARCNOW_MCP_NETWORK
names (default arc-testnet, so nobody is pointed at real money by omission), or from a document the
operator names in ARCNOW_MCP_NETWORK_FILE. Moving this pin is therefore how the addresses this server
sends money to change - and this move is the one that made arc-mainnet resolve at all.
WHAT CHANGED IN THE SURFACE, and what it meant for the tools:
- No developer share. FeeConfig/FeeSplit/PlatformSettings/NewPlatform carry creator, platform, ref and
protocol only; `developer` is gone from BuyRequest, SellRequest and Trade's requests;
previewFeeSplit(fee, referrer?) and platformShareBps(creator, ref). Every tool schema lost its
`developer` argument (a strict schema now refuses one by name), arcnow_register_platform lost
devShareBps, and every fee breakdown prints FOUR parties. arcnow.io's split is 3000/1000/3500/2500.
- Pool fees are the hook's: POOL_TRADE_FEE_BPS 80 (0.80%) beside POOL_LP_FEE_PIPS 2000 (0.20%),
POOL_TOTAL_FEE_BPS 100; Pool.fees() -> { hookFeeBps, lpFeePips, totalBps, split } read off the hook
(feeBps(), feeConfigOf()) and the key. Every pool report - arcnow_token, arcnow_quote_buy/sell,
arcnow_buy/sell in a pool - reads its rates from Pool.fees() and holds no fee constant; the retired
hook that charged 1% in the pool is refused as UnknownHookVersion. feeQuote on pool quotes and fills,
buyFeeFromQuoteIn and sellFeeFromQuoteOut are at 80 bps.
- Launching is free: LAUNCH_FEE_WAD 0 on every quote of both networks. The tools keep printing the
registry's figure (launchFee on LaunchQuote, QuoteRegistryEntry, protocolSummary) and say 'launching
is free' when it is zero, rather than assuming it.
- Version gates accept 4.x and refuse 3.x BY NAME as the retired multi-quote stack (its testnet data
was wiped); 2.x and 1.x are refused as before. assertHookVersion is exported; the fake uses it.
- CurveTemplate.reference() is the mainnet template (1,000,000,000 supply, 50,000 to graduate);
arcnowDefaults() is testnet's (1,000,000 / 50); referenceFor(network) picks per preset, which is
what arcnow_register_platform seeds a new platform with. ArcToken.VERSION() is arc-token@2.0.0.
- FeeShare { Creator 0, Platform 1, Ref 2, Protocol 3 } is exported; not used here yet.
Still used from it, unchanged: QuoteAmount and QuoteTokenInfo, which label every amount with its own
quote; CurveState.quoteToken; quoteIn/quoteSpent/quoteOut/feeQuote on quotes and results;
Pool.quoteToken() and quoteIsCurrency0(); LaunchQuote {quoteToken, launchFee, initialBuy, totalCost,
nativeValue, tradeFee}; approvalTxHash on buy, pool-buy and launch results; client.quoteRegistry.list(),
client.quoteToken(info).spendState and client.quoteTokenInfo; findQuoteToken, NETWORKS and
resolveNetwork; platforms.curveParametersFor; the codes QuoteTokenMismatch and
QuoteAmountNotRepresentable; QuoteTransferOutOfGas; erc20GasLimit (estimate plus max(20%, 150,000));
withPoolQuoteTransferHeadroom (estimate plus max(20%, 400,000)); GRADUATION_GAS_LIMIT and
GRADUATION_GAS_FLOOR; and the SDK's WrappedError unwrapping for a revert inside the pool.

$comment: Restated here so this repository can be read alone, and asserted against
the SDK's networks.json by the test suite so the two can never drift into
disagreeing. Addresses are NOT restated: they live in the SDK's
networks.json and are read from it at run time. Two copies of an address
list is how one of them ends up wrong. The SDK ships two presets, arc-testnet
and arc-mainnet (chain 5042, rpc.mainnet.arc.io); what is pinned below is the
one the FORK PROOF forks, which is testnet. The suite asserts both presets.
Arc's gas currency IS USDC and msg.value is an 18-decimal integer. The
6-decimal figure belongs to the ERC-20 interface predeploy, which is the
same asset and does not pay for gas. Everything this server prints says
which of the two it means.
fork_block is the Arc testnet block the fork proof forks at. Pinned, so
anvil caches the state it fetches (test/fork/support/chain.ts mounts its
cache) and a repeat run asks the rate-limited public endpoint for nothing
it already has. The proof DEPLOYS ITS OWN fee-model (4.x) stack onto the fork
with the private SDK checkout's fork deployer and points the server at it
through ARCNOW_MCP_NETWORK_FILE, so no arcnow.io address on the forked chain
is read and the block does not have to be after the deployment of the live
testnet stack (62386232). What it does have to carry is what the proof
borrows from Arc: EURC, the v4 PoolManager, the v4 router, and real EOAs in
the 400 blocks before it to impersonate. 61926859 carries all four and is
already in the cache, which on a rate-limited endpoint is worth more than
resembling today's tip. ARCNOW_MCP_FORK_BLOCK overrides it; "latest" forks
the tip.

toolchains.$comment: Exact, never a range and never auto-detected - the same node release arcnow-io/sdk pins, because this server runs the SDK that toolchain built.

images.$comment: Pinned, never 'latest'. The anvil the fork proof runs: the same Foundry image arcnow-io/sdk and arcnow-io/e2e-tests pin, so a fork that behaves differently in one of them behaves differently for a reason somebody chose.
